title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Let X be a topos and u: Z -> Phi a monomorphism of abelian sheaves with Psi = Coker u. Assume: (a) Psi is Z-flat; (b) for i>0 the sheaves Gamma^i Phi and Lambda^i Phi stay flasque after tensoring with any abelian sheaf, hence Gamma^i Phi (x) Lambda^j Psi is flasque for i>0. Set K_u = Gamma*_Z Phi (x) Lambda*_Z Psi. It is the divided-power Koszul complex of 0 -> Z -> Phi -> Psi -> 0. Its differential is the PD-derivation that is the canonical map Phi -> Psi on Phi and zero on Lambda Psi. With T |-> 1 in Z = Ker(Phi -> Psi), it is a resolution of the divided-power polynomial algebra Z{T} = Z<T>. After base change to any sheaf of rings k, K_{u,k} = Gamma_k Phi_k (x) Lambda_k Psi_k resolves k<T>.

This page. K_{u,k} is bigraded by:
- the exterior degree j (from Lambda^j);
- the total degree, or weight, n = i+j on Gamma^i (x) Lambda^j.
The differential d raises j by 1, keeps n fixed, and lowers the complementary degree i by 1. With the weight grading, K_{u,k} is a graded algebra over the graded ring k<T>; in fact it is a sheaf of strictly graded-commutative dg algebras with divided powers.

The weight-n piece is 0 -> k.T^[n] -> Gamma^n Phi -> Gamma^{n-1} Phi (x) Psi -> ... -> Lambda^n Psi -> 0. It is exact. All terms are flasque except possibly the last, Lambda^n Psi (the i=0 term). Write K(X,u,k) = Gamma(X, K_{u,k}) and H^{n,j}(X,u,k) for its cohomology.
- For j<n, H^{n,j} = H^j(X,k), by flasqueness.
- For j=n, apply the long exact sequence to 0 -> Z^{n-1} -> F^{n-1} -> Lambda^n Psi -> 0, using H^1(F^{n-1}) = 0 and H^1(Z^{n-1}) = H^n(X,k). This gives Coker(Gamma F^{n-1} -> Gamma Lambda^n Psi) = H^n(X,k), so H^{n,n} = H^n(X,k) as well.
- For j>n the complex is zero.

Hence the Theorem: the augmentation H^{**}(X,u,k) -> H^*(X, k<T>) = H^*(X,k) (x)_Z Z<T> is an isomorphism in bidegrees (n,j) with j <= n, and H^{n,j} = 0 for j > n. This is the triangular region drawn in the corner picture. Equivalently, H^{**}(X,u,k) = (+)_n tau_{<=n} RGamma(X,k) . T^[n], a divided-power Rees module of the canonical (Postnikov) filtration.

The relative corollary for a morphism of topoi f: X -> Y states that f_* K_{u,k} -> Rf_*(k<T>) = Rf_*(k) (x) Z<T> is an isomorphism (on cohomology sheaves) in bidegrees j <= n, with zero for j > n. The next page rephrases this as an isomorphism with a truncation and then studies functoriality in u: maps lambda: Phi -> Phi' with lambda u = u' induce quasi-isomorphisms, and two such maps differ by Theta with Theta u = 0, leading to homotopies.

Purpose: to produce, functorially in X and k, a strictly commutative divided-power dg-algebra model of the cohomology of a topos over an arbitrary base ring (e.g. Z or F_p). The price is the weight variable T and the truncation j <= n. The obstruction to strict commutativity (Steenrod squares) is absorbed by T: (x T)^2 = x^2 T^2 = 2 x^2 T^[2] vanishes mod 2, consistent with x^2 = 0 for odd x in Lambda. This belongs to the 'complexe de De Rham a puissances divisees' programme, the de Rham/PD side of the schematization problem later formulated in Pursuing Stacks.
errors: The flasqueness used is only for i>0. Lambda^n Psi (i=0) need not be flasque; if it were, every H^m(X,Z) with m >= 2 would vanish, already from the weight-1 piece. The isomorphism in the extreme bidegree j=n therefore needs the short extra argument via H^1 of the cycle sheaf. Grothendieck states it without comment, but it is correct.

Notation 'bidegree (i,j)' on this page means (weight = total degree, exterior degree), whereas on the previous page i was the Gamma-degree. This is potentially confusing but consistent with the claim j <= i.
Statement 'the differential of the first member is zero for j>i' (next page): in fact the complex itself vanishes for j > weight. Harmless.

Multiplication by T is not the transition map of the canonical filtration: on H^j . T^[n] it is (n+1) times the inclusion of tau_{<=n} into tau_{<=n+1}. The structure is a divided-power Rees module, not the ordinary Rees module. This is not an error, but it is worth noting since the page calls K a graded algebra over k{T}.

ideas.what: Divided-power Koszul complex Gamma Phi (x) Lambda Psi of 0->Z->Phi->Psi->0 as a resolution of the divided power algebra Z<T>
ideas.modern_name: PD Koszul complex / Gamma-Lambda Koszul resolution (Illusie, Complexe cotangent I, Ch. I §4.3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Koszul, Cartan); in this form Illusie 1971; Quillen

ideas.what: Bigrading by weight n=i+j and exterior degree j; global sections compute H^j(X,k) for j<=n and vanish for j>n, i.e. a weight-graded model of the truncations tau_{<=n} RGamma
ideas.modern_name: (Divided-power) Rees construction of the canonical/Postnikov filtration; filtered derived category, décalage
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (décalage, Hodge II, 1971), Beilinson (filtered derived), later Bhatt-Lurie / Simpson-type Rees constructions

ideas.what: Strictly graded-commutative PD dg-algebra model Gamma(X, Gamma_k Phi_k (x) Lambda_k Psi_k) of cohomology of an arbitrary topos over an arbitrary ring k, functorial up to quasi-iso in the choice of u
ideas.modern_name: Strictly commutative (divided-power) cochain models; commutative cochain problem over Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational), Mandell (E_infinity cochains), Karoubi (quasi-commutative cochains), Toën (affine stacks / schematization)

ideas.what: Relative version: f_* K_{u,k} models Rf_*(k) (x) Z<T> in the triangular range j <= n
ideas.modern_name: Relative truncated PD-algebra model of Rf_*

missed.claim: A strictly commutative dg algebra with divided powers on any topos and over any base ring, graded by a divided-power variable T. Its weight-n part computes exactly tau_{<=n} RGamma(X,k). The truncation and the T-divisibility (T^2 = 2T^[2]) make strict commutativity compatible with the Steenrod obstruction over Z and F_p.
missed.quote: Muni du degré total ... K est une Algèbre graduée sur l'Anneau gradué k{T}. ... ceci est un isomorphisme pour les bidegrés (i,j) tels que j≤i, tandis que H^{i,j}(X,u,k)=0 ... pour j>i.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The obstruction to commutative cochain models over Z is central to schematization (Toën's affine stacks) and to integral rational-homotopy analogues. A filtered/Rees-type strictly commutative PD model of cochains is a nontrivial device; I do not know it to be in the literature in this form or credited to Grothendieck.

missed.claim: The output is a divided-power Rees module of the canonical filtration, with multiplication by T acting as (n+1) times the transition map. This links Grothendieck's 1976 PD-de Rham programme to filtered/Rees techniques (décalage, filtered derived de Rham, conjugate filtrations with divided powers in Bhatt's work, filtered circle / G_m-equivariant constructions).
missed.quote: H^{**}(X,u,k) --> H^{**}(X,k{T}) ≃ H^*(X,k)⊗Z{T} ... On peut l'exprimer comme un isomorphisme des 1ers membres avec un certain tronqué du second
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modern treatments of the conjugate/Hodge filtrations on derived de Rham cohomology use Rees algebras over Z[t] or divided-power variants. This page shows Grothendieck using a PD-weight variable to encode Postnikov truncation, an early form of that idea.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra (PD Koszul resolution, flasque computation) is routine, but using it to obtain a strictly commutative PD-dga, weight-graded by T, that models exactly the canonical truncations of cohomology of an arbitrary topos is a notable unpublished construction relevant to the commutative-cochain and schematization problems. It is not dramatic, and close relatives (Rees constructions, PD Koszul complexes) are standard.
